svg.title: The goalie's stick at the two nets, NHL '94 Genesis
svg.text: The goalie's stick isn't the same at the two nets (NHL '94 Genesis)
Where his stick blade is comes from a table, one point per sprite frame. The bottom goalie faces up the screen and uses different frames, and their points aren't the top goalie's mirror image.
1. As drawn on screen (red dot: the blade point the game uses)
2. Both nets drawn the same way (the bottom one flipped top to bottom), goalie 19 out, to scale
Top: blade 6 out, 1 to the right
Bottom: blade 7 out, 0 to the middle
Top: blade 4 out, 11 to the right
Bottom: blade 6 out, 4 to the right
Top: blade 7 out, 7 to the left
Bottom: blade 1 out, 6 to the left
within 8 of the blade: a low puck is caught or knocked away
8 to 14 from the blade: the blind ring, a low puck passes untouched and his body isn't checked
Low puck = height 5 or less, not rising. Blue: the top net's goalie; orange: the bottom net's. Points for a goalie drawn as stored; one drawn mirrored (by his hand) flips the side at both nets alike.

The blade decides which low shots he stops, and the blind ring beside it lets some through. With the two nets' blades in different spots, the same low shot can be stopped at one end and slip through at the other.
Measured: NOSE4Web's recorded shots replayed at both nets against the computer goalie (1,027 paired): Down/Up 1.03 on retail,
1.00 with the bottom goalie's points mirrored from the top's (NOSE4Web's "Bottom goalie's stick fix").
A small effect, about 3% more goals at the bottom net, within chance on its own; in the league it is one of several small asymmetries behind the 1.03 Down lean (docs/img/updown_genesis.svg).
